The world

TETRAA single world · A thousand stories

One world turning on the four-sided die, all four faces charted and mapped.

Water
At least half of every face
Edges
Land and sea continue across every edge
Size
20,000 miles from the corner of Spikia, straight through the world, to the base of Mount Celestial. Worked out from that, not yet Ruby’s word: about 24,500 miles along each edge.

The calendar

Months
13 · 28 days each. Counted Ruby’s way, from March, September, October, November and December are the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th months and Tredesember the 13th; the strip below runs that way, with January, February and Tredesember at its end, after the Restart Day.
Year
364 days + the Restart Day, which is one and a quarter days long: 365¼ days, so there are no leap years. The year begins on 1 January. The Restart Day closes it, between December and the next January, and the rain comes with it; on the strip, New Year comes round in the middle, sort of, as Ruby puts it.
Week
7 days: Starday, Moonday, Goldday, Blueday, Spikeday, Wetday, Twilightday. A month is exactly four weeks. That the year begins on a Starday and the Restart Day stands outside the week, so that every month runs from a Starday to a Twilightday, is a reading, not yet Ruby’s word.
One day
One full turn · 25 hours
Spin
Leftward
Years
Counted from year 0. There is a year -0 as well, and it is not the same year as 0. The years before run backwards, the way BCE does on Earth.
Now
Year 1700. In technology, about Earth’s 1750.
The weekAs proposed and accepted: Starday for the star, Moonday for the d3 moon, Goldday for the magical field whose light flows like gold, Blueday for the magnetic field, Spikeday for Spikia, Wetday for Wetia, Twilightday for Mount Celestial.

Seasons on the Canon Face · on average

    A slower turn, a richer world.

    The two fields

    Magical field · slows lightGoes all the way around the world. It slows light, so dawn crosses the land slowly and the first light comes in gold, and it turns the dark purple star’s light into the colour of our own sunlight.Here, the morning moves slower. And light flows like gold.
    Magnetic field · guides worldsGoes all the way around the world too. It guides worlds.

    The star

    A dark purple starTetra’s sun is a dark purple star. Its light reaches the ground the colour of our own sun’s light, because the magical field turns it on the way in. It stays level with the middle of the world, never higher and never lower, so every place has as much bright as dark, and on Mount Celestial it sits on the horizon all year.

    The moon

    A d3 moonTetra’s moon is a three-sided die, a d3, and not the cube kind: one crater on its one side, two craters on its two side, three craters on its three side. It is a fair die (Ruby: “a fair d3 for tetra”): a rounded three-sided rod whose ends come to points, so it can only ever come to rest on one of its three sides. It is a third of the size of Tetra, circles a little farther out than the magical field, and rolls slowly so every side comes round. Every ordinary day it sits on the opposite side from the star, drifting gently about that spot. Every month, in the middle of the month, is the new moon: the die swings round in front of the star and the world goes dark, a solar eclipse. Its light waxes and wanes through the month like our own moon’s, full when the month turns, and the Restart Day is never a new moon. While the die covers the star, every place on Tetra reads “Eclipse”, day side and night side alike.

    The four faces

      The Dice System

      Worlds beyond chance. Tetra is the four-sided world and Cuba the cube planet; they share this page, and the buttons under the title switch between them.

        Different worlds. Same imagination.

        Life of Tetra

        The Umbrella Tree Zinnia

        A single tall stem that is not wood, crowned with a wide umbrella of broad petals. Small blossoms hang on threads from the rim of the crown.

        It grows in magical places with a lot of water, most of all in Wetia and on the West Face.

        There are more of them on Cuba than here, since there is more magic there (Ruby).

        Ruby: “add most of the recognizable plants from the real world to bouth”. So most of the plants you would know from Earth grow on Tetra too, for example oaks, pines, birches, maples, willows, palms, bamboo, cactuses, ferns, mosses, grasses, clover, dandelions, daisies, roses, sunflowers, lilies, lotuses, wheat, corn, rice, apple trees, cherry trees, orange trees and strawberries. Which grows where is unwritten. Ruby: “anything that grows on tetra also grows on cuba”, so all of these grow on Cuba too.

              Facing · The Canon Side

              The world

              CUBAThe cube planet · The Dice System

              A world with six square sides, the second world of Ruby’s Dice System after Tetra.

              Sides
              Six, named like Tetra’s with two more: Canon, East, West, Far, North and South. North is the top and South the bottom. Looking at Canon, East is on its left, West on its right and Far behind it.
              Drawn so far
              The Canon side: the Plus Continent, whose four arms reach the sides and connect onto the East, West, North and South sides, with the Canyon in its middle, the small hole that takes you through the world to the Far side. The Far side, from Ruby’s words of 2026-10-05, “the far side has a main island about a quarter of the sise of the face with land on the north east and south east corners, making it half water. on the central island, north of the canyon, there is a volcano (active) (shoots lava every reset day)”: the main island around the Canyon’s other end, land on the north-east and south-east corners, half water, and the volcano north of the Canyon, erupting every Restart Day. The North, East, South and West sides (2026-10-06): drawn from Ruby’s sketches of the explorers’ maps (Aquamarine, Axinite, Benitoite, Chrysoberyl), with the Plus Continent’s arms reaching in as far as the sketches show. Nothing on those four sides is named yet.
              Size
              About 20,000 miles from one end of the Canyon to the other, probably: as long as Tetra is from the corner of Spikia through to Mount Celestial (Ruby). The Canyon runs straight through, so that is the length of every edge (a reading).
              Turn
              The same way as Tetra, leftward, and a day the same length as Tetra’s: one full turn, 25 hours.
              The star
              Tetra’s dark purple star, seen from farther out. It stays where it is: turn the world to find it, as Ruby asked.
              Tetra
              Visible in Cuba’s sky as a small four-sided world toward the star (Ruby: “you shuld be able to see tetra from cuba and vice versa”); where exactly it stands is a reading.
              Fields
              One magical and one magnetic, both a little stronger than Tetra’s (Ruby): the gold and blue rings around the world, hidden only where the world itself is in front of them.
              Place
              Farther from the star than Tetra. Ruby: “if there were 5 magical fields, and tetra was in the first one, cuba would be in the last one (going away from the star would be the direction they were stacked in)”.

              The calendar

              Months
              14 · 28 days each: Tetra’s thirteen and Amberary, the fourteenth, placed between January and February (Ruby). Counted Ruby’s way, from March, the strip below runs that way, with January, Amberary, February and Tredesember at its end, after the Restart Day.
              Year
              392 days + the Restart Day, which on Cuba is one and a half days long: 393½ days, “same as tetra but probably one month longer”. The year begins on 1 January, after the Restart Day, as on Tetra.
              Years
              Counted from Amber’s landing: “when amber reached cuba, she clled it year one of cuba (so rigt now it is year 50)”. It is year 50 of Cuba while it is 1700 on Tetra.
              Week
              Seven days with Tetra’s names: Starday, Moonday, Goldday, Blueday, Spikeday, Wetday, Twilightday (Ruby: “same names for days on cuba also”). 392 month days are 56 weeks, so with the Restart Day outside the week every month runs from a Starday to a Twilightday (a reading, as on Tetra).
              One clock
              Tetra and Cuba share their days: a day here is a day there, and pausing, spinning or stepping time on one does it on both. Their years and months are their own, so when Tetra steps from Tredesember into March, Cuba is just starting Tredesember.
              Amberary
              “half in rain seoson half in transition between rain and spring” (Ruby): the first fourteen days are rain season, the last fourteen the time between rain and spring.
              Seasons
              The rain season runs through the Restart Day, January and the first half of Amberary; then the time between rain and spring; then spring from February. The months from February on have Tetra’s seasons (Ruby, 2026-10-06: “same as tetra”). In the rain season it rains on every side (Ruby), though never on the moon or the star.

                The moon

                “the moon of tetra is similar to cuba” and “a d5 probably” (Ruby). So Cuba’s moon is Tetra’s in every way but the die: a five-sided die, a third of Cuba’s size, circling a little farther out than the magical field, opposite the star on ordinary days, swinging round in front of the star on the 14th of every month for a solar eclipse, rolling once a day, waxing and waning through the month. Ruby first allowed “the round shape used for equal oucomes in the real world, or is just a square piramid”, then wrote “te piramid does not grant equal chances so whatever grants equal chances for bouth moons is good” and “a fair d3 for tetra and a fair d5 for cuba”. So the d5 is a fair d5: a five-sided long die, a pentagonal rod with one to five craters in a row along each of its five long sides, and pointed ends, so it can only ever come to rest on a side. That it is a rod rather than another fair shape is a reading.

                Life of Cuba

                Ruby: “add most of the recognizable plants from the real world to bouth and add more umbrela tree zinias on cuba than on tetra (cince there is more majic)”, and “anything that grows on tetra also grows on cuba”. So everything that grows on Tetra grows here, most of the plants you would know from Earth among them, for example . The Umbrella Tree Zinnia, whose stem is not wood and whose top is petals, grows here more than on Tetra, since there is more magic. Ruby, 2026-10-06, on which plants grow where: “i don't know yet (earth planets grow all over)”, so Earth’s plants grow all over Cuba, and the colours of the land are Tetra’s (“same as tetra”).

                The Montezuma. Ruby: “cuba has a gian tree called montezuma that grow ut to a 15th of the hight of mount celectial”. Then: “it grows to be 1 mile high and 1.5 mile radius in canopy and a 3/4 mile wide trunk it will grow on the east side of cuba when it is writen”. So: a giant tree of Cuba, a mile high, with a canopy a mile and a half in radius and a trunk three quarters of a mile wide, growing up to a fifteenth of the height of Tetra’s Mount Celestial; it will grow on the East side once that side is written, and nothing is drawn until then (the East side is drawn from her sketch since 2026-10-06; whether that is “writen” enough for the tree is hers to say). Her two lines together make Mount Celestial fifteen miles high, which does not fit the mountain in the build (0.6 of the moon’s length, far taller); which to keep is hers to say. Whether it is one tree or a kind of tree, and whether it also grows on Tetra, is unwritten.

                The Plus Continent and the Canyon

                From Ruby’s picture of the Canon side (2026-10-04): a broad island shaped like a cross, with an arm toward the middle of each side and rounded bends at the corners. In the middle she wrote “to far side”: the small hole that takes you to the opposite side of the world. Ruby: “the arms connect to the north south east and west faces”, so the land crosses those four edges; how far it goes on each of those sides she does not know yet (2026-10-06: “i don't know yet”); it is drawn as far as her sketches of the explorers’ maps show. The island’s shape is drawn from the description of her picture. Ruby named them: “the hole is called the canyon, the island is called ‘the plus continent’”. And “you can come thugh the hole ither way, so the far side will probably get explored next”.

                How Cuba was reached

                “lets imagine that amber the explorer makes a chamber out of a tree and (calculated corectly) launches of ither spikia or the far side using majic, gets flung by the moving moon (going in or out of solar eclipse) gets flung by the star and lands on the cannon face of cuba (year 1650)”

                Ruby, 2026-10-04, in her words. Amber the explorer, in a chamber made from a tree, launched by magic from Tetra, flung on by the moving moon at an eclipse and then by the star, and landed on the Canon side of Cuba in the year 1650. She launched from Tetra’s Far side (Ruby: “8: far side”).

                The explorers

                Ruby: “5 people also came with amber, they are all explorers: Ammolite, Aquamarine, Axinite, Benitoite, and Chrysoberyl (they are for exploring the other sides when we get there)”. Then: “ammolite has desided to go down the canyon”, and “Ammolite has drawn a map and is heading back down to the cannon side”. Her map has not reached the page yet. On 2026-10-06: “North side explored by aquamarine”, “East side discovered by axinite the explorer”, “South side discover by benitoite the explorer”, “Chrysoberyl is waiting until she’s done resting”, “Chrysoberyl’s map of west side”, with her sketches of those four sides, which the sides are now drawn from.

                  Still unwritten

                  • How far the Plus Continent’s arms go on the East, West, North and South sides: Ruby, 2026-10-06, “i don't know yet”; they are drawn as far as the explorers’ sketches show them.
                  • Names: the Far side’s (Ruby: “i don't know yet”), and everything on the four sides, which her sketches leave unnamed; and what the spiral on the North side and the dark mark on the West side are.
                  • Which plants grow where beyond Earth’s: Ruby, “i don't know yet (earth planets grow all over)”, read as Earth’s plants growing all over Cuba.
                  • Mount Celestial’s height, which Ruby’s two Montezuma lines make 15 miles and the build makes far more.
                  • What Ammolite’s map shows, and whether it is the Far side as drawn here.

                  Everything above comes from Ruby’s words and from the description of her picture. The photo itself has not been checked against this drawing yet. Cuba shares this page with Tetra, as Ruby asked; the buttons under the title switch between the two worlds.
